checked_sources: RESULT.md; verify.py; verified Git tree a1dff888039d313efecb8c05eeb7ab0cdcd75891
Independent implementation of graph blue forcing and all proper-subset fort inclusion tests, every subset n=2..7; full polynomial and counts exact.
correctness.rationale: For all integer n>=2, each initially blue A_i has exactly a+1_{i in W_B} white neighbors and blue B_i has b+1_{i in W_A}; the exhaustive cases a=0 or b=0 or singleton white layer with a nonmatched blue forcing witness give a necessary-and-sufficient success condition. Counting the cases yields the all-coefficient zero-forcing polynomial, Z_n(1)=(n+1)2^(n+1)-n^2-6n-1 for n>=3, and minimum count 2n(n-1)+2. Fort constraints classify a,b: singleton-versus-(n-1) sets and two-plus-two sets, with n=2/3 exceptions; combinatorial proof all n. Independent direct full graph simulation/fort inclusion tests for n=2..7 exactly reproduced every reported polynomial and minimal fort histogram (including 44 degree-four forts at n=4). Poisson white-count convergence proves the independent-failure window, not correlated cases.
residual_risks: Random robustness limit is only for independent Bernoulli initial blue colors.

evidence: The zero forcing polynomial of a graph (https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.08910): Defines polynomial and known extremal coefficients; not the entire K_n square K2 enumerator.
